body:
I get asked every day why all of this happened. Simply...Why? Seven years ago, an advisor closely witnessed Matt Tyrmand’s behavior alongside me while

[](http://email.alert.keepcongressrepublican.com/c/eJyEkE-LpDAQRz9NvCllSiMePCyIt97rHqVMau2g-UMSd5lvP9hDw9zmWr_Hg1d_HuuD7Gn9_pscT4dOa8qr29bg9pr1M3BeJciuBlnDuLaVmcyoFamKp3aAoW9B9WP1nEhL0w1DSxugIYV925GGrcdemX5jrOx0e0DCKAGhUw0aZIPAKFvsNjCiAzo5leZgjjr4PXHOieO1nVaTb3Rw1Tk9S4lZ4C8hFyGXzPpK3JBnE8pNCLmEg_kvOzaW9hSuKORC3tt_nDKlj9ptdQyRBC5XcWsOV9IscP6GCKnu6TZcTuD8wr9umlwku3uB87vmvQRf2BeB86FTlSYT_9vztFkNooPdkT1fAeXnF38GAAD__3P8hAU)

[](http://email.alert.keepcongressrepublican.com/c/eJyEkE-LpDAQRz9NvCllSiMePCyIt97rHqVMau2g-UMSd5lvP9hDw9zmWr_Hg1d_HuuD7Gn9_pscT4dOa8qr29bg9pr1M3BeJciuBlnDuLaVmcyoFamKp3aAoW9B9WP1nEhL0w1DSxugIYV925GGrcdemX5jrOx0e0DCKAGhUw0aZIPAKFvsNjCiAzo5leZgjjr4PXHOieO1nVaTb3Rw1Tk9S4lZ4C8hFyGXzPpK3JBnE8pNCLmEg_kvOzaW9hSuKORC3tt_nDKlj9ptdQyRBC5XcWsOV9IscP6GCKnu6TZcTuD8wr9umlwku3uB87vmvQRf2BeB86FTlSYT_9vztFkNooPdkT1fAeXnF38GAAD__3P8hAU) Dear Friend,

This week is the one-year anniversary of Matt Tyrmand and his friend Dan Strack leading a 6-hour Maoist "struggle session"-style board meeting flogging me for taking SUVs to meetings, stealing pregnant lady's sandwiches, and, amongst other things, claiming I'm a terrible leader. I have a recording of that meeting that I never released.

Matt Tyrmand said Project Veritas didn't need James O'Keefe anymore and would be fine without him. That, along with his statement, "You didn't build that, your employees did," sounded right out of the Labor theory of value, one of the pillars of Marxism. He seemed to want the farm without the farmer or the golden eggs without the goose that produced them. This is a common problem with nonprofits in general. Nobody owns anything; therefore, no good deed goes unpunished - if you have the wrong people involved.

My main concern in the board meeting one year ago tonight, while I sat there quietly being flogged for hours, was indemnifying our journalists because I knew the organization would run out of money if they voted me out. That action would leave our journalists, who needed defending, hung out to dry. The ongoing lawsuits affected 1st and 4th Amendment principles, particularly unconstitutional FBI raids and accompanying search warrants. I never settle lawsuits on principle because I refuse to bear false witness on the 1st amendment and choose the challenging, expensive route of dying on every 1st amendment hill. I can only do this by making the final decisions about raising and apportioning money to litigation. Our cases remain in the circuit courts, with some inevitably bound for the Supreme Court. Since making these final decisions and having the backs of our journalists is central to the sanctity and integrity of the journalism itself, my journalism and being the CEO and final decision-maker are inextricably linked.

So, I had no choice but to ask the board to resign. They refused. They also refused to consider or even fathom the indemnification issue. The "struggle session" indicated they weren't even interested in dialogue. They informed me I needed to take my lashings and feel remorseful. The board eventually resigned months later, anyway, after they spent millions of dollars and ran out of money. It wasn't until then that they started to confront the indemnification issue (you can ignore reality, but you can't ignore the consequences of ignoring reality) and began to send out emails asking their audience to pay the legal bills of those raided. Then, to the shock of the few remaining Project Veritas staff, leadership used the little money they raised from the fundraising emails not to support legal defense but to pay themselves. This irresponsible conduct was so unconscionable that it led to their own lawyer's resignation.

After being fired, I had the impossible task of somehow raising funds to pay Project Veritas journalists' legal bills while starting a new venture (OMG - O'Keefe Media Group) from scratch and with absolutely no infrastructure. If that wasn't impossible enough, Project Veritas - the company I founded- sued me and asked a Federal Judge in New York to issue an injunction to stop me from working. Now, things started to seem demonic.

This led most of Project Veritas' donors and audience to believe the worst-case scenario - that people were compromised, pinched, or worse. While that is certainly possible, I don't know that to be true. However, the timing did provide undeniable circumstantial evidence. What did Matt Tyrmand, Dan Strack, George Skakel, John Garvey, and Joe Barton think people would be going to assume after taking such a drastic action of 'indefinitely suspending" James O'Keefe only a week after the Pfizer story?

Donors and the audience were going to conclude that the Project Veritas Board was evil, stupid, or compromised.

Then, in a late May board meeting, a day after Dan Strack quit, there was a stand-off where staff demanded Matt Tyrmand resign after he said he wanted to "carve out James heart and eat it in front of him." I have a recording of that meeting and have not released it. George Skakel, previously an ally of Tyrmand, wrote a letter demanding Tyrmand resign or be fired. Tyrmand resigned in July and promised that dirt on James O'Keefe would come out to the media. Under his brief leadership, Matt Tyrmand managed to burn through the $10 million I raised before being fired. After I left, almost nothing was raised, and donors demanded their money back. Matt also hired a new CEO who fired the entire staff before she, too, quit.

Coincidentally, there was a police report filed over stolen checks around the time that happened, and people are still trying to get to the bottom of that.

Over the last year, Matt Tyrmand has sent pornographic posts and sexually harassing text messages that are so obscene I can't post them or describe them here without the risk of being banned on this platform. I still do not understand why a person would be compelled to do that.

Matt Tyrmand's initial strategy, when asked by people what he was thinking, was the somewhat effective "Adam Schiff approach" -"James has done something terrible, but I can't tell you what it is. It will come out later." This approach was used on Trump regarding Russia by Congressman Schiff. In my case, it worked on some people until they learned that Matt had already released everything he had. Whatever he knew, he would leak and share immediately. To this day, the standard response from those responsible for the destruction of Project Veritas is, "You don't know what you're talking about." When asked what they mean, no new justification or evidence is given. All that is provided are insults, pornographic images, and slurs. I have hundreds of these communications saved from some former employees and board members who often use anonymous phone numbers and X accounts.

I get asked every day why all of this happened.

Simply...Why?

Seven years ago, an advisor closely witnessed Matt Tyrmand's behavior alongside me while we were on his boat. One day, the advisor pulled me aside and warned me that Tyrmand "wants to be you, James. He's jealous of you." Looking back, I was oblivious to it, and the events described above would have been inconceivable in my mind back then. Again, I was raised to believe in the best in people. Someone taking a more Hobbesian approach to human nature would not have founded Project Veritas or chosen my path.

The lesson here is how jealousy and envy can destroy a man in the worst way and destroy organizations and even movements. It is a disease in our politics, institutions, economics, and humanity. Envy is the root of all socialism. Envy has led to death and destruction throughout the 20th century. Envy is inherent in human nature and one of the things we fight against.

It is a spiritual battle, a tale as old as time.

This was the anniversary of that fateful board meeting when I was escorted out of the building in tears, a building that my sister, an architect, helped me construct and design back in 2015. A building that was flooded and destroyed and had to be rebuilt again back in 2021 in the face of constant defamation, raids, and lawsuits. Things can be destroyed in a moment. It takes so much time to build.

But I am grateful to have the overwhelming toxicity entirely removed from my life. The cancer is all gone. I am liberated now. My greatest mistake was not firing Dan Strack immediately when he told me in the Summer of 2022 that he would not follow my lead. I commit to you, my audience, to never make that mistake again.

There is more to say, but at the moment, I have more pressing things to do, like producing our story for Wednesday about yet another institution we infiltrated. Footage you wouldn't believe unless you saw.

And see it you will, 4 pm - 6 pm, every Wednesday, "ON THE INSIDE w/ James O'Keefe"...Tune in then, and **[any support you can offer to continue our mission is, as always, greatly appreciated](http://email.alert.keepcongressrepublican.com/c/eJyEkE-LpDAQRz9NvCllSiMePCyIt97rHqVMau2g-UMSd5lvP9hDw9zmWr_Hg1d_HuuD7Gn9_pscT4dOa8qr29bg9pr1M3BeJciuBlnDuLaVmcyoFamKp3aAoW9B9WP1nEhL0w1DSxugIYV925GGrcdemX5jrOx0e0DCKAGhUw0aZIPAKFvsNjCiAzo5leZgjjr4PXHOieO1nVaTb3Rw1Tk9S4lZ4C8hFyGXzPpK3JBnE8pNCLmEg_kvOzaW9hSuKORC3tt_nDKlj9ptdQyRBC5XcWsOV9IscP6GCKnu6TZcTuD8wr9umlwku3uB87vmvQRf2BeB86FTlSYT_9vztFkNooPdkT1fAeXnF38GAAD__3P8hAU).**

In Truth,

James O'Keefe
Founder and CEO
O'Keefe Media Group

Hi there,

I want to share more about my late husband, Grant Woods, and how he inspired my pursuit of public service.
[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/78722580/454260306/-401216107?refcode=em-2.9.24-all-a&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNTkvMS8xMDYwODgiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiYTBiYzI3ZmYtOGFjNy1lZTExLTg1ZjktMDAyMjQ4MjIzNzk0IiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=qUpsBvf6dikRCkGRCa7K9OWpdLueIJ6ZXQ8iZPnQo5g=)
I met Grant in 1988 when I moved to Arizona to work at Channel 12. A friend asked to set me up on a blind date with a Republican. After covering the GOP convention as a reporter, I was nervous, to say the least.

Before I agreed, I asked if he was at least pro-choice. He was so I said yes. He was also hilarious, and brilliant and irreverent. Best blind date ever. The rest, as they say, is history.

Service was Grant’s guiding light and he was elected Attorney General of Arizona in 1990. Arizona was his home. He was committed to justice and believed it was his responsibility to “look out for the little guy”. That's why he went to law school to begin with, and it's why he was such a dynamic Attorney General for our state - always putting country over party and people over politics.

You can only imagine how much the kids and I have missed Grant these last 2 years. Some days the grief still takes my breath away. But here’s what I do know: I am who I am today because of him. I’m proud of his voice, his impassioned work and his legacy to make our state and our country better. As I continue my campaign to serve Arizona, I am filled with comfort and strength knowing I carry with me his lessons and passion for public service.

[**I hope to inspire this community the way my husband did by putting service to Arizonans at the center of everything we do. That's what our community deserves, and if you’re with me, please consider making a $3 donation today.**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/78722581/454260307/-401216107?refcode=em-2.9.24-all-a&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNTkvMS8xMDYwODgiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiYTBiYzI3ZmYtOGFjNy1lZTExLTg1ZjktMDAyMjQ4MjIzNzk0IiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=qUpsBvf6dikRCkGRCa7K9OWpdLueIJ6ZXQ8iZPnQo5g=)

clean_body: | = Hi there, I want to share more about my late husband, Grant Woods, and how he inspired my pursuit of public service. = I met Grant in 1988 when I moved to Arizona to work at Channel 12. A friend asked to set me up on a blind date with a Republican. After covering the GOP convention as a reporter, I was nervous, to say the least. Before I agreed, I asked if he was at least pro-choice. He was so I said yes. He was also hilarious, and brilliant and irreverent. Best blind date ever. The rest, as they say, is history. Service was Grant’s guiding light and he was elected Attorney General of Arizona in 1990. Arizona was his home. He was committed to justice and believed it was his responsibility to “look out for the little guy”. That's why he went to law school to begin with, and it's why he was such a dynamic Attorney General for our state - always putting country over party and people over politics. You can only imagine how much the kids and I have missed Grant these last 2 years. Some days the grief still takes my breath away. But here’s what I do know: I am who I am today because of him. I’m proud of his voice, his impassioned work and his legacy to make our state and our country better. As I continue my campaign to serve Arizona, I am filled with comfort and strength knowing I carry with me his lessons and passion for public service. = Thank you, Marlene | **=** | Marlene's campaign to flip AZ-01 is being built from the ground up with grassroots support! = To learn more about Marlene and how she's fighting for Arizona families, please visit: We'd hate to see you go, but you can click here if you'd like to . | | I’d like to take a moment to reintroduce myself. I’m Lauren Groh-Wargo, and in 2018, I worked with this incredible community to launch Fair Fight with the mission of defending and repairing our democracy by fighting voter suppression. Since then, that work has included waging critical legal battles, building a statewide and national infrastructure to fight voter suppression and support voting rights, and bringing together a network of strong supporters — all working together to achieve our mission. Key to our efforts have been two landmark lawsuits that highlighted the sustained attacks on voting rights and engagement in Georgia, each with national implications. These lawsuits became multi-year efforts, drawn out by multiple national crises and complicated by a changing legal landscape — including devastating Supreme Court decisions and new state laws restricting voting access that together have stripped judges of the authority to adequately protect voting rights. While our mission and moral obligation charged us to continue pursuing legal relief and protection on behalf of voters, the costs of these efforts have outstripped our projections. These costs have unfortunately come at a time of contraction in funding resources that has affected many groups in our space, making our current trajectory unsustainable. While these realities are disappointing, we are not discouraged. With your support, Fair Fight has greatly advanced the pro-democracy agenda, pushed back and mitigated the impacts of voter suppression, and realized important wins and gains for all Americans. **Last week, we announced changes to our organization that allow us to hone our mission and adapt to serve Georgia and American voters for the 2024 cycle and beyond. Our objectives are clear:**
* **Refocus:** We will target Fair Fight’s activities on the core functions of voter protection, communications, and operations.
* **Restructure:** An organizational restructure is underway. We are reducing our current team and realigning staff and resources to align with our mission. While difficult, this is critical to ensure the long-term viability of Fair Fight and to ensure a meaningful impact in the months and years ahead. We are working closely with our team to support them in every way possible during this transition, and know they will continue to make important contributions to this cause and many others.
* **Reorganize:** At the Fair Fight Board’s request, I have stepped up as Interim CEO to steward the reorganization and work with the team on developing and advancing the strategy. Cianti Stewart-Reid has resigned as Executive Director and will be pursuing other opportunities. We are grateful for all of her contributions and commitment to Fair Fight and its mission over the last three years.

**Our goal is to revise the operating model so that Fair Fight is strongly positioned for the battles ahead. Our core mission remains: to fight back against those who seek to disenfranchise voters and take away our freedom to vote and live the lives we choose as Americans. Their attacks continue to spread and escalate, so our commitment must be unwavering.** **I would also like to take this opportunity to thank you and everyone who has supported Fair Fight over the last six years with your time, energy, resources, and financial contributions.** Together, we have made tremendous progress, and the work continues. I will be in touch as we chart our course to hear your thoughts and share our plans. [**In addition, I need to ask: If you’re in a position to make a donation right now, can you help launch this new phase of our work on the strongest possible footing with a contribution of $10 or any amount? Your dollars would make a real difference at this moment as we regroup and gear up for the rest of 2024 and beyond.**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/78724588/454268586/-1128031810?amount=10&refcode=bsc_emm_ff_20240209_f_announcementNOR_v1s2&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNDMvMS84ODQ1MCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJkYzc1ZmJkYS04ZmM3LWVlMTEtODVmOS0wMDIyNDgyMjM3OTQiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=ccQqTniMQitfe6tIrTP98UpAuyp9TD1rVcMWoBGKRqc=) With a strong commitment to continuing the Fight and a deep gratitude to this community, Lauren Groh-Wargo

Derek, a grifter who is now under trial is speaking to the NRA convention tonight in Harrisburg -- **and no, I don’t mean the former head of the NRA, I mean Donald Trump.**

body:
As Governor, I will work to address the teacher shortage, contend with learning loss, and make effective investments in Virginia’s public schools.

| [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/78726020/454273959/1044321784?refcode=BLU_EM_ASFG_2024-02-09_1&amount=25&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMjQvMS8xMDM4NTgiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiOTYwMGRmMmYtOTNjNy1lZTExLTg1ZjktMDAyMjQ4MjIzNzk0IiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=Ti2IL-GgNbocBKDnhumxvPzF8Y0c0gMvnTIhrrTkBxo=)

| Peter,

As a mom of three school-aged children here in Virginia and a proud product of Virginia public schools, I know that our public education system is one of the most important tools we have to set our kids up for success.

We need to make sure our public schools have the resources they need — and we need to recognize the value of teachers' hard work, focus on strengthening our workforce training programs, and support Virginia's extraordinary higher education institutions. And we need to stop creating divides that distract from our top priority: building a stronger Virginia for the next generation.

As Governor, I will work to address the teacher shortage, contend with learning loss, and make effective investments in Virginia’s public schools.

**The success of every child in Virginia — as well as the success of our workforce and entire economy — depends on the success of our schools. clean_body: As Governor, I will work to address the teacher shortage, contend with learning loss, and make effective investments in Virginia’s public schools. | = | Peter, As a mom of three school-aged children here in Virginia and a proud product of Virginia public schools, I know that our public education system is one of the most important tools we have to set our kids up for success. We need to make sure our public schools have the resources they need — and we need to recognize the value of teachers' hard work, focus on strengthening our workforce training programs, and support Virginia's extraordinary higher education institutions. And we need to stop creating divides that distract from our top priority: building a stronger Virginia for the next generation. As Governor, I will work to address the teacher shortage, contend with learning loss, and make effective investments in Virginia’s public schools. The success of every child in Virginia — as well as the success of our workforce and entire economy — depends on the success of our schools. This was a modified bill, after an earlier one that included anti-immigrant policies failed to pass this week. Please call your Senators before they vote again very soon to officially pass this legislation. And in the House of Representatives, a bill that would have sent $17.6 billion to Israel’s military got a majority of votes, but failed to meet a special two-thirds voting threshold. That’s too close. Many of our government’s leaders don’t seem to see people of Muslim faith or Arab heritage as human beings. They’re deeply disconnected from the people they’re supposed to serve, millions of whom are demanding a ceasefire. Instead of funding our communities’ needs, many of my colleagues in Congress continue to funnel billions of dollars to defense contractors—which many of them are invested in and taking campaign donations from. The bill failed, because it needed a special two-thirds majority to pass. Yesterday, most Senate Democrats voted for a bill that would send $14.1 billion to Israel’s military to drop more U.S. bombs on Palestinian children. The bill would also have blocked U.S. funding for the UN agency supporting millions of Palestinian refugees with life-saving aid—all while the Israeli government intentionally starves people and attacks supply trucks heading into Gaza. The bill, which Biden supported, included far-right U.S. border policies that would end asylum protections, lock up more refugees, and speed up mass deportations. These cruel anti-immigrant policies were included as an attempt to get Republican support on the bill, which ultimately failed. Sadly, most of our government’s leaders don’t seem to see immigrants or people of Muslim faith or Arab heritage as human beings. Although this week’s legislation didn’t pass, Democrats and Republicans in Congress are going to keep trying to hand over billions of American taxpayer dollars to Netanyahu’s genocidal regime. As the only Palestinian American in Congress, I will continue to speak up , no matter how many times my colleagues try to censure me or police my words. I can’t stand by while the U.S. arms and enables genocide. My district’s residents sent me to Congress to invest in life, not death and destruction. Their demands echo the demands of the American people. Every day, more cities and labor unions representing millions of Americans are joining the call for a ceasefire. More U.S. leaders need to listen and to recognize our shared humanity. Congress recently passed$886 billion for this year's Pentagon budget, and yesterday the Senate considered a $118 billion package for war and xenophobia. Instead of funding our communities’ needs, many of my colleagues continue to funnel billions of American tax dollars to the very same defense contractors that many of them are invested in and taking campaign donations from. That's why I just introduced legislation to stop members of Congress from profiting financially when they vote to support wars and weapons manufacturing. We deserve better. Taking the lead from grassroots movements, I'm working towards a federal government that ends poverty, that values diplomacy and peace over the military industrial complex, and that finally creates a real path to citizenship for our immigrant neighbors. We're building a future where instead of funding war, our government funds housing, healthcare, utilities and clean water, childcare, climate solutions, reparations for Black Americans, education, and more for our communities. Members of Congress should be accountable to the people. That's who I'm here to serve. | | _"A sympathetic, well-meaning, elderly man with a poor memory.”_ These are not [the words](http://links.burchettforcongress.com/u/click?_t=feefb5ad83f24ba4b99ac997c1b47e86&_m=2c99232e592647eb9a3dfb4ea9a50d23&_e=DuwG8ikxUj8zasr1KwMTbhXc7wheiuxr8S2EHoNMMC1lSbVHd8WFX2Mj0kn-4KDnMwfUfVrNeXlLKt_8Ial23wdl6CZ1dav4tRcljUueW2kvNobLN68fSOxq0WSHvyiMDaukp7MIIlleIp1oOrrseZDEJz7O7u_dAsgkI6NwYenP9805rV4NTHOSxSd8HCbjhbQB4Z55d7Ue30Y18PUM8YJlTHdEFVROOzf4NCflTqMuiK2zE7714TLTE5i-hXXsmu_zOLfYayzQsWmeRjVoQ6ZOd9BJdimFlRcjigw496X6N7_y2-YnXDilrutF-thesEBUcrg3Ocwht2AVbz_qJA%3D%3D) that should be used to describe our nation’s leader and commander in chief, yet that’s exactly where we find ourselves, folks. Special Counsel Robert Hur, tasked with digging into Biden’s [improper handling](http://links.burchettforcongress.com/u/click?_t=feefb5ad83f24ba4b99ac997c1b47e86&_m=2c99232e592647eb9a3dfb4ea9a50d23&_e=DuwG8ikxUj8zasr1KwMTbhXc7wheiuxr8S2EHoNMMC0FiRazKWiIY5-8h5fkjxk3CZEpuhLmQReo4uNFVyDbG6GSSglzhkZE8OiJSkTIRh84WQBc8zo27A_XIxdVnyXqd9x_Akrwq6Ly2ZUVQD1dGtRBcl4OQCYU7ZibvIjiFUFoRQSzmSjlG1q5Fvr5GeQtmmfRIaR2oIWd11sQPw6VHE5-DeJ7DMKlTmaPDYJW7JDmVxOps_SviBIwr4UAZQLeXpTbbNwJ-aT7TPhWPGFfUybPI4J-T8NUEbTrFavPCeU%3D) of classified records, announced yesterday that he won’t recommend criminal charges against the president. But that’s not the headline—especially because we all saw it coming from a mile away. The real story is that the Left is finally admitting what we’ve known all along: 81-year-old President Biden is [not competent](http://links.burchettforcongress.com/u/click?_t=feefb5ad83f24ba4b99ac997c1b47e86&_m=2c99232e592647eb9a3dfb4ea9a50d23&_e=DuwG8ikxUj8zasr1KwMTboK4wCbgze2BNT5cmiYWeFoyY4WfWxX7ZI_9M9-kGqAlPq3jYIrrjwzMCgf4twAp1Csh4k8yAerAxVNmI1S-vOpc1FPU-z8g5I-g__OacnDe8LZxpdiK69zOFqgCyZORqi0lj8iV3S-sEr_QXZSxCvBZ4awXDqH0-t7dGUwPEG8j5M4Z1xAEZ9PVkjAGBuoS-HhoJeUPuPG42vQMNoj80jKu08R0wfi2PHOhGTGtJ-J73fUGgy11qL5t5COCw8C4f4068Y8JrbJHHmlA8sTh1_eb0OwAnGbFNsVRYlO02HnY) enough to be the leader of the free world. Election Day will be here before we know it, and it’s becoming increasingly clear that [Americans are unsure](http://links.burchettforcongress.com/u/click?_t=feefb5ad83f24ba4b99ac997c1b47e86&_m=2c99232e592647eb9a3dfb4ea9a50d23&_e=DuwG8ikxUj8zasr1KwMTbiP5GXedrOovPpZtKH30iyAV-Z37aaxV4hVEMh61SCFY-L5YOwYAu9C1oj12dYkRie4wBlDx8A_Y44Wq5DOmh-TgZjcExdP3vADsdoAQU_ZF7fUyG8Avu6f_Yk6aGk-szPdt_RhtLu3fUziRSWFtnhNcAUNt6LeaaiYBkNQIjfxbypdr9QLF9fO1Xd10vS1h_iKDCr0okdyZ6BxgtelPjzKfty0Lo_5N2Tu4hOyiNSPxHwx9JTlUr2vgMfrKaydZHoyWioVH-nJ7DJVKt6dWj0-jAjrivb7QnrdexqjIl7Ek) of whether Biden is up to the job. Weiss's Relationship with Conservative Backers Under Scrutiny | | | [View this email in your browser](https://mailchi.mp/889982d77379/pro-choice-paradox-joanna-weisss-alleged-abortion-rights-stance-at-odds-with-conservative-cash-influx-15670320?e=7017cc100e)

| | **For Immediate Release:** February 9, 2024
**Contact:**[press@davemin.com](mailto:press@davemin.com)
**Pro-Choice Paradox: Joanna Weiss's Alleged Abortion Rights Stance at Odds with Conservative Cash Influx**
_Weiss's Relationship with Conservative Backers Under Scrutiny _
**IRVINE, CA** — Already under scrutiny for self-funding her campaign with a fortune made from defending the Diocese of Orange County against a slew of sexual abuse lawsuits, Joanna Weiss faces new questions from Democratic voters over discrepancies between her purported pro-choice platform and the hundreds of thousands of dollars in support she is receiving from outside dark Republican money. Recent revelations regarding Weiss's financial backers and patterns of alignment with right-wing figures have ignited a firestorm of concern, calling into question her integrity and commitment to progressive values.

**“Joanna Weiss's actions speak louder than her words,”** said Dave Min campaign manager Dan Driscoll. **“While she claims to champion progressive values, her decision to fund her campaign with tainted money earned from defending the Catholic Church against sexual abuse lawsuits raises serious ethical questions. Now, with the revelation of her cozy relationship with dark Republican money, it's clear where her loyalties lie. Democratic voters deserve a candidate who stands unwaveringly for their values, not one who sells out to the highest bidder.”**

The United Democracy Project, acting as AIPAC's independent expenditure arm, has pledged extensive resources to bolster Weiss's bid while actively opposing State Senator Dave Min—a stalwart abortion rights supporter backed by the California Democratic Party and esteemed Representative Katie Porter. AIPAC's track record of endorsing far-right, MAGA-aligned Republicans like Elise Stefanik and Jim Jordan starkly contradicts Weiss's alleged pro-choice advocacy. The alliance underscores a disturbing trend of Weiss associating herself with politically distasteful actors, further eroding trust among Democratic constituents.
**_Here is a List of the Top Donors to the SuperPac Boosting Joanna Weiss_** **$5,000,0000 from GOP megadonor Jan Koum**
* In 2023, Jan Koum Contributed $5M To SFA Fund, Inc., A PAC Supporting Republican Presidential Hopeful Nikki Haley
* Haley has characterized her position as “unapologetically pro-life” and [confirmed](https://davemin.us7.list-manage.com/track/click?u=1b97cb6a343b55cba640c3404&id=f1c2af9ef3&e=7017cc100e) to the New York Times that she would have signed a 6-week abortion ban as governor of South Carolina.

**$2,500,000 from GOP megadonor Jonathan Jacobson**
* 2010-2014: Jonathan Jacobson contributed $136k to the National Republican Senatorial Committee. According to the Public Accountability Initiative’s Little Sis project, Jonathan Jacobson contributed $136,000.00 to the NRSC between 2010 and 2014. [Public Accountability Initiative, LittleSis, Accessed 2/6/24].
* The National Republican Senatorial Committee is run by Republican Senator Steve Daines – founder and chair of the Senate Pro-Life Caucus – and is the main arm of the Republican Senate campaign, pouring millions into supporting anti-Choice MAGA candidates such as Senator Ted Cruz, Senator Josh Hawley and Senator Rand Paul.

**$1,000,000 from Home Depot Co-Founder Bernie Marcus**
* In 2022, Marcus gave $1,000,000 to support Anti-Abortion MAGA Republican candidates such as Brian Kepmt and Doug Mastriano through the Republican Governors Association
* Also in 2022, Marcus gave $250,000 in 2022 to support anti-Choice attorneys general such as Texas’ Ken Paxton and Kansas’ Kris Kobach – two of the most aggressive anti-abortion attorneys general in the United States
* Marcus Defended Steve Bannon as a ‘passionate zionist and supporter of Israel’ [Haaretz, 6/27/22]

**$1,000,000 From Hedge Fund Manager And Pro-Trumper Paul Singer**
* Singer, 77, is a hedge fund manager who founded Elliott Management Corporation and has an estimated wealth of over $4 billion.
* Singer donated significant amounts to a pro-Trump super PAC and the Republican National Committee, [Haaretz, 6/27/22]
* In 2022, Singer Contributed $750,000 to the Republican Governors Association, which supported anti-abortion candidates like Brian Kemp and Doug Mastriano.
* The RGA’s 2022 slate of endorsed candidates included Gov. Brian Kemp of Georgia, who signed a 2019 ‘heartbeat’ bill that bans abortions after about six weeks of pregnancy, one of the most restrictive anti-abortion laws in the country.

**$500K From GOP Donor Michael Leffell**
* According to the [Federal Election Commission](https://davemin.us7.list-manage.com/track/click?u=1b97cb6a343b55cba640c3404&id=53655db1ed&e=7017cc100e), the United Democracy Project accepted $500,000.00 from Michael Leffell in 2023-2024.
* Also in 2023, Michael Leffell contributed $10,000 to the House GOP Battleground Fund
* House GOP Battleground Fund is run by Congresswoman Elise Stefanik, who called those serving time for the January 6th insurrection “[hostages](https://davemin.us7.list-manage.com/track/click?u=1b97cb6a343b55cba640c3404&id=b24f605003&e=7017cc100e)”

The fallout from the [Daily Beast’s](https://davemin.us7.list-manage.com/track/click?u=1b97cb6a343b55cba640c3404&id=a91051664a&e=7017cc100e) shocking investigative report on candidate Joanna Weiss’ self-financing of her campaign with over $230,000 for a fortune earned in part by representing the Catholic Church against sex abuse, child molestation and sexual assault claims in Orange County continued last Friday in a news story by [Politico](https://davemin.us7.list-manage.com/track/click?u=1b97cb6a343b55cba640c3404&id=d2285b6515&e=7017cc100e), in which Joanna Weiss’ campaign pushed back on the Daily Beast’s findings stating that Weiss “primarily represented the [Catholic] diocese on employment matters.” ###

_California’s 47th is an open Congressional District in Orange County that includes the Cities of Costa Mesa, Huntington Beach, Irvine, Newport Beach, and Seal Beach, and portions of Laguna Beach, Laguna Hills, and Laguna Woods. Incumbent Katie Porter is vacating the seat to run for U.S. Senate. In 2022, Porter defeated former Assemblymember Republican Scott Baugh by 3.44% in this “toss-up” district. State Senator Dave Min currently represents over 80% of Congressional District 47 in Sacramento. In 2020, Min received over 158,000 votes within CA-47, defeating incumbent John Moorlach by 5.15% in this area. 19% of the registered voters in CA-47 are of Asian and Pacific Islander descent, including one of the largest Korean-American populations in the country. _

I’m leading the fight right now to pass paid family and medical leave in Virginia.

[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/78728614/454281679/-1514006159?refcode=email-header&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTMvMS84NzQ0NCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI0MzdhY2E3My05YmM3LWVlMTEtODVmOS0wMDIyNDgyMjM3OTQiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=r3AU_X0MiId9geJC0XIwve9QXdYhzxDmDpF0XPgR1LU=) For far too long, people have been forced to make the incredibly difficult decision of caring for someone they love or skipping a paycheck.

Women in particular are hard hit by this challenge because we also often are the de facto caregivers for our families and for our loved ones.

It is long past time that we stand up for workers and make sure they have the ability to take care of their families when they need it most.

**That’s why I’m leading the fight right now to pass paid family and medical leave in Virginia. And that’s the exact kind of change I’ll fight for in Congress too.**

Virginians deserve leaders who understand the challenges they face every day and are willing to stand up for them. But look, making paid family leave a reality – whether it’s in the state legislature or in Congress – takes a major grassroots effort.

**[That’s why I’m reaching out to you today. To pass paid family leave for every American, we need to win this battleground race for Congress and take back the House. body:
Last year, I joined the Michigan State Senate and a funny thing happened

[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/78729361/454284360/1433120897?refcode=email-header&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMzMvMS85NjAyNCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJjMzg3YWUxNS05ZmM3LWVlMTEtODVmOS0wMDIyNDgyMjM3OTQiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=tLeyy2M-8L9Kg3DxzvTm857VQCmXNgANGAhw80-kIbo=) Last year, I joined the Michigan State Senate and a funny thing happened. Together with my Democratic colleagues, we made meaningful change for Michigan residents. And today, I want to tell you about one of my proudest moments in the legislature so far: **Last year, we passed the largest tax break for working families in Michigan’s history.** You read that right. We worked together to pass legislation and now, 700,000 working Michigan families will receive checks of roughly $3,200 to help them pay for basic necessities like food and childcare. Over __1 million children__ live in households eligible for these checks. I’d been fighting for the Working Families Tax Credit for years because working families struggling to get by need one thing: money in their pockets. And I’ll be honest, it wasn’t an easy fight. But we got it done, not by pointing fingers or playing political games, but by bringing together a broad coalition of community members and leaders who want every Michigan family to be able to thrive. That’s the same approach I’ll take in Congress. Now more than ever, we need leaders who will actually try to work together to get things done. From investing in education to getting more money into families’ pockets to protecting our reproductive rights, we can’t afford any more inaction. [_**That’s why I’m running for Congress, and why I’m asking for your support. This race won’t be easy either – the House GOP’s top Super PAC already said our district is a “top priority” to win – but I know if we build a broad coalition once again, we will win. | | Good news this week, Friend. President Biden's EPA just released a stronger standard for soot pollution that **will protect thousands of people from asthma and air pollution-related deaths each year.** **This is your win.**
The initial draft of the rule did not go far enough, so **over 11,000 of you** stepped up to submit a public comment to the EPA,**** joining a national movement of advocates speaking out to protect our communities.

**We specifically called for the new, stronger standard of 9 micrograms per cubic meter** , which research shows will prevent 4,500 deaths per year and hundreds of thousands of other medically related events. **Thank you for taking action with us on this critical rule.** We are grateful that EPA has taken necessary action on soot. Now, the administration must turn their attention to the remaining air quality standards.

subject: Read this ASAP: House prepares to force MASSIVE expansion of climate-destroying gas exports
body:
Time sensitive

Peter - our Membership Drive deadline is a few days away, and we're reaching out because we haven't heard from you yet (renew your membership here and your contribution will be tripled https://links.messages.lcv.org/els/v2/EZ_ ).

The truth is your membership matters, and it's particularly critical right now.

Here's the situation: Earlier this month, Senator Joe Manchin backed away from a climate deal after months of negotiations, choosing to side with Big Oil and Republicans. It leaves the deal one vote short -- stalling any real action in Congress for now.

In response, we're redoubling our efforts on pushing the White House to act decisively on climate. The Biden administration has massive amounts of power to curb climate pollution - but that will only happen if the environmental movement makes it happen.

Right now, we're facing a critical test: the Biden administration is weighing a plan to block all new oil and gas drilling leases on public waters.

This could be huge -- and a decision is coming. Right now, we're organizing volunteers from all over the country to flood the administration with letters, pressuring Biden to hold to his promises.

Peter -- it's your membership support that makes victory possible here. But we have to do more. A group of donors has put together a fund to triple match every contribution before Sunday's membership deadline:

Can we count on your support? Claim your membership now - it only takes $5 >> https://links.messages.lcv.

The ban on new oil and gas leases is the first of many huge environmental decisions, Peter. And right now, we're pushing for serious action on so many fronts -- including:
Setting tight standards for power plants and other major emitters of climate pollution
Placing strict limits on air pollution to safeguard all communities Expediting requirements of 100% tailpipe pollution-free new cars by 2035 and trucks by 2040
Protecting communities from hazardous and super-polluting methane Conserving 30% of our public lands and waters by 2030 Declaring a climate emergency - and so much more. The best way you can help win each and every one of these fights right now is to claim your LCV membership - all it takes is a gift of $5 or more. https://links.messages.lcv.org/els/v2/dmyWFAmK~DF_

Thank you, thank you, thank you, Peter. This is such a critical moment for the environment, and we're so fortunate to have you on the team.

Onward,

Gene Karpinski
President

The truth is your membership matters, and it's particularly critical right now. Right now, we're organizing volunteers from all over the country to flood the administration with letters, pressuring Biden to hold to his promises. body:
|
# [](https://act.adamschiff.com/go/61?t=1&akid=5261%2E5257348%2EQHppwG)

Hi Derek,
It’s Robert De Niro.
**We need Adam Schiff to be California’s next U.S. Senator.[If you agree, please support his campaign today by pitching in any amount. ](https://act.adamschiff.com/go/1014?c0=feb2024_abs_em.yNAKTE&refcode=AU_ABS_FR_GEN_EGR_AC90_20240209_PM2_V1_S1&email=&t=5&akid=5261%2E5257348%2EQHppwG)**
From his position as one of the leaders of the House of Representatives, Adam has been on the frontlines of the fight to protect and preserve our democracy for years. He’s stood up to bullies like that small-time wannabe tough guy Trump. I want to see Adam take his might into the Senate to face down other cowardly bullies like Cancun Ted Cruz and Fist-Pump Josh Hawley.
Adam has shown the resolve to take on big challenges in our government and to make the reforms necessary to get it working for the American people.
He’s for abolishing the filibuster, expanding the Supreme Court, and overturning _Citizens United_ to get big money out of politics. And that’s the key we need to unlock progress on a host of other issues — from reproductive freedom to voting rights to LGBTQ+ equality and climate action, and so much more.
**[If you’re ready to join me in sending Adam to the United States Senate, then show it by chipping in – any amount – to support his campaign ahead of his primary election. Adam is running against 26 candidates of all parties in just a few weeks, and he needs your help.](https://act.adamschiff.com/go/1014?c0=feb2024_abs_em.yNAKTE&refcode=AU_ABS_FR_GEN_EGR_AC90_20240209_PM2_V1_S1&email=&t=6&akid=5261%2E5257348%2EQHppwG)**

Our country is at a crossroads. We are under threat from Trump and his Senate enablers.
We need Adam Schiff in the Senate fighting to save our democracy.
Thank you.
Robert De Niro

name: Elissa Slotkin
subject: Black History Month in Michigan
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY ELISSA SLOTKIN FOR MICHIGAN
body:
# [](https://act.elissaslotkin.org/go/188?t=1&akid=1120%2E135344%2EwbqJs4)

Friend -
In honor of Black History Month, I want to take a minute to talk a little bit about local Black history here in Michigan and particularly the role Detroit played in our national story. Detroit’s geography, being just a 2,400-foot boat ride from Canada, helped make us a major Underground Railroad destination in the United States, with the code name “Midnight” for escaped slaves from the South. Here are some of the important milestones most people don’t know.
In 1833, before Michigan had become a state, hundreds of Black Detroiters and white abolitionists joined together to break a Black husband and wife out of prison in Wayne County. They succeeded in transporting the couple by boat to Canada. It was a galvanizing point, and the ringleaders of the uprising went on to found the Second Baptist Church, the oldest Black church in Michigan and a stop on the Underground Railroad. It’s estimated that 50,000 escaped slaves settled or stopped before the final leg of their journey across the Detroit River into Canada.
In 1869, a member of the same Second Baptist Church, Fannie Richards, who was working as a teacher joined a lawsuit, _Workman v. Detroit Board of Education,_ challenging mandatorily-segregated schools in Detroit. They won and opened an integrated public school in 1869, 85 years (!) before _Brown v. Board of Education._
In the 1910s and 20s, the Great Migration brought more than 100,000 Black residents to Michigan, seeking good jobs and an escape from the Jim Crow regime in the South. But they encountered racist practices when they arrived, with redlining, racially restrictive covenants, and discriminatory Homeowners Associations enforcing segregation for decades.
Nevertheless, Black Michiganders worked towards equality and justice. The Second Baptist Church, 119 years after its founding, was the largest financial donor to the Montgomery Bus Boycott in 1955, the event kicked off by Rosa Parks refusing to give up her seat. Parks later moved to Detroit, where she spent decades working in politics and activism, including to dismantle racist housing practices.
This is just a tiny snippet of Michigan’s Black history. I encourage you to explore Michigan’s Black history, not just this month, but year-round. Take a trip to the Motown Museum, the Charles H. Wright Museum of African American History, or the Henry Ford Museum (where you can tour the actual bus Rosa Parks sat in.) Visit one of the many monuments to the Underground Railroad in our state, or make a stop at a Black-owned business.
Happy Black History Month!
Elissa

clean_body: Friend - In honor of Black History Month, I want to take a minute to talk a little bit about local Black history here in Michigan and particularly the role Detroit played in our national story. Detroit’s geography, being just a 2,400-foot boat ride from Canada, helped make us a major Underground Railroad destination in the United States, with the code name “Midnight” for escaped slaves from the South. Here are some of the important milestones most people don’t know. In 1833, before Michigan had become a state, hundreds of Black Detroiters and white abolitionists joined together to break a Black husband and wife out of prison in Wayne County. They succeeded in transporting the couple by boat to Canada. It was a galvanizing point, and the ringleaders of the uprising went on to found the Second Baptist Church, the oldest Black church in Michigan and a stop on the Underground Railroad. It’s estimated that 50,000 escaped slaves settled or stopped before the final leg of their journey across the Detroit River into Canada. In 1869, a member of the same Second Baptist Church, Fannie Richards, who was working as a teacher joined a lawsuit, Workman v. Detroit Board of Education, challenging mandatorily-segregated schools in Detroit. They won and opened an integrated public school in 1869, 85 years (!) before Brown v. Board of Education. In the 1910s and 20s, the Great Migration brought more than 100,000 Black residents to Michigan, seeking good jobs and an escape from the Jim Crow regime in the South. But they encountered racist practices when they arrived, with redlining, racially restrictive covenants, and discriminatory Homeowners Associations enforcing segregation for decades. Nevertheless, Black Michiganders worked towards equality and justice. The Second Baptist Church, 119 years after its founding, was the largest financial donor to the Montgomery Bus Boycott in 1955, the event kicked off by Rosa Parks refusing to give up her seat. Parks later moved to Detroit, where she spent decades working in politics and activism, including to dismantle racist housing practices. This is just a tiny snippet of Michigan’s Black history. I encourage you to explore Michigan’s Black history, not just this month, but year-round. Take a trip to the Motown Museum, the Charles H. Wright Museum of African American History, or the Henry Ford Museum (where you can tour the actual bus Rosa Parks sat in.) Visit one of the many monuments to the Underground Railroad in our state, or make a stop at a Black-owned business. Happy Black History Month! Elissa PAID FOR BY ELISSA SLOTKIN FOR MICHIGAN P.O.
